findings.description: setOne(projectId, subscriberId, CustomFieldType type, String key, Object value) is now present.
findings.detail: Signature matches the tech-spec exactly (line 88 of SubscriberCustomFieldsService.java). type==null guard returns immediately (no-op skip, line 89-90). Non-null path calls validateAndNormalize then delegates to applyAll via singletonMap (lines 92-93). No audit call inside setOne — responsibility is documented (Javadoc, lines 68-87) and explicitly left to the caller. Controller does NOT route through setOne; it continues to use the two-pass validateAndNormalize+applyAll with a single aggregated recordCustomFieldsSet call (controller lines 85-97). All-or-nothing controller semantics are fully intact.

findings.description: validateAndNormalize null-type guard is now in place.
findings.detail: Lines 58-60: if (type == null) throw new IllegalArgumentException("type must not be null"). Unit test validateAndNormalize_nullType_throwsIllegalArgument confirms it (SubscriberCustomFieldsServiceTest lines 64-70).

summary: Both round-2 findings are fully resolved. CF-R2-01: setOne is present with the exact spec signature; null-type returns immediately (no-op skip); non-null path validates then applies via singletonMap; no audit is written inside the method and this is clearly documented. The controller continues to use the independent two-pass validateAndNormalize+applyAll path with one aggregated recordCustomFieldsSet call, so all-or-nothing semantics and the sole-writer audit invariant remain intact. CF-R2-02: validateAndNormalize now throws IllegalArgumentException on a null type argument, with a corresponding unit test. All four TDD anchor tests for setOne are present and cover valid, deleted-skip, invalid-422, and null-unset cases. No new issues found. Implementation is clean and production-ready.
